items.title: Sebi approves transfer of ICICI Securities' PMS biz to ICICI Prudential AMC
items.rss_summary: Market regulator Sebi has approved the proposed transfer of portfolio management services (PMS) business of ICICI Securities to ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company. The proposed acquisition will be carried out through a slump sale on a going-concern basis. "We hereby inform you that the company is in receipt of an email today... from ICICI Securities intimating receipt of a letter dated November 19, 2026, from Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) approving transfer of PMS business from ICICI Securities to the company," ICICI Prudential AMC said in a stock exchange filing on Thursday. The company's board of directors approved the acquisition of the PMS business from ICICI Securities on August 10. Subsequently, both companies entered into a business transfer agreement for the transaction. The closing of the transaction was subject to receipt of requisite regulatory approvals. items.title: Tata Technologies aims to double its revenue by $1.3 billion by 2030
items.rss_summary: Tata Technologies Ltd, which provides product engineering and digital services to manufacturers, aims to double its revenue to USD 1.1-1.3 billion while expanding operating profit margin to more than 20 per cent by 2030. The company is betting on multiple large full-vehicle projects, software services and the aerospace and industrial heavy machinery segment. Its revenue in FY26 was around USD 600 million with an EBITDA margin of 15.5 per cent. The company is expecting revenue to grow in double digits in current financial year FY27 and to expand further at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 15-20 per cent between FY27 and FY30, according to an investor presentation. items.title: Blackstone stake buy to boost IIFL Finance's capital needs: Fitch Ratings
items.rss_summary: Blackstone's plan to acquire a 16 per cent stake in IIFL Finance will support the Indian firm's growth capital with an unlikely shift in IIFL's business model, which focuses on secured loans, Fitch Ratings said on Thursday. Fitch said with the investment, Blackstone would effectively become IIFL Finance's main private-equity shareholder. Fitch believes that the refreshed shareholder and board composition could alter IIFL's business strategy, risk appetite and growth trajectory. However, the significant injection of capital and foreign investment supports Indian financial institutions' capital and funding flexibility. Earlier this month, the board of IIFL Finance approved a plan to raise Rs 6,414 crore through a preferential issue. This included Rs 5,000 crore investment from Blackstone and Rs 1,264 crore by the company's promoters Nirmal Jain and R Venkataraman, besides Rs 150 crore from Anchorage Capital.
